phase_0.domain_name: The tuple occupies R0 through R3 alone as four pairs, and R4 through R7 belong to the closure witnesses, so the adjoint and the one-to-one do not enter the register file.
phase_0.boundary_condition: the register file boundary, separating data registers R0–R3 from witness registers R4–R7, with the adjoint and one-to-one excluded from the file entirely

VINIT.chosen_element: vacuum state of the register file before any tuple is loaded
VINIT.justification: the system begins in a void where no data or witness slots are present; all eight registers contain N

TANCH.chosen_element: the architectural specification that the register file is eight-wide, with the lower four holding tuple pairs and the upper four reserved for closure witnesses
TANCH.justification: this boundary closes the system, determining what may enter each register block and what is permanently excluded from the file

AFWD.chosen_element: loading the IG tuple into the computational substrate
AFWD.justification: the tuple moves from an external representation into the machine, populating the eight data slots (D,Φ,T,Ω,K,f,H,P) into R0–R3 as four B4 pairs

AREV.chosen_element: removal of the adjoint and one-to-one slots
AREV.justification: the four slots R, Γ, Ç, Σ are actively discarded before register assignment; they are pulled out of the tuple stream and not written to the file, ensuring the file contains only data pairs

CLINK.chosen_element: chaining of tuple ingestion with slot selection and witness inscription
CLINK.justification: the operations form a linear composition: void → load tuple → split into data and witness slots → select data slots → write data registers → inscribe witnesses → vote → record

IMSCRIB.justification: the running program computes four closure witnesses (token diversity, self-reference, Frobenius order, dialetheia completeness) and writes them into R4–R7, conferring identity on the system and making its closure evidence accessible for subsequent evaluation

FSPLIT.chosen_element: decomposition of the full IG tuple into all twelve slots
FSPLIT.justification: the tuple is split into two sets: the eight data slots destined for R0–R3 (D,Φ,T,Ω,K,f,H,P) and the four witness-ancillary slots (R,Γ,Ç,Σ) that are excluded from the register file

FFUSE.chosen_element: recomposition of the data slots into the original tuple
FFUSE.justification: the eight data slots are fused to recover the identical IG tuple that was loaded, verifying that the register file content suffices to reconstruct the tuple without the adjoint and one-to-one; the constraint FFUSE(FSPLIT(x)) = x holds because the excluded slots are redundant for tuple identity in this architecture

EVALT.chosen_element: successful exclusion of witness-ancillary slots from the register file
EVALT.justification: the T-branch of the split evaluates to true when the four excluded slots are absent from R0–R3; the file contains only clean data pairs, ready for closure witness inscription

EVALF.chosen_element: inclusion of adjoint or one-to-one in the register file, violating the architectural boundary
EVALF.justification: the F-branch represents a state where witness-ancillary slots enter R0–R3, corrupting the data block and mixing tuple content with closure evidence; this branch is never taken but must exist for the split to be well-formed

ENGAGR.chosen_element: the unresolved moment during split when both inclusion and exclusion of ancillary slots are simultaneously possible
ENGAGR.justification: before the architectural constraint is applied, the system entertains a paradice where R, Γ, Ç, Σ both are and are not part of the register file; this dialetheia collapses to the true branch when the boundary rule asserts that they do not enter

IFIX.chosen_element: permanent recording of the substrate vote result
IFIX.justification: the token scores computed from the register file are fixed in append-only memory, creating an irreversible record of which token the substrate selects for program synthesis; this mirrors the kernel’s snapshot tier determination

phase_2.split_input: the tuple as loaded from the Grammar, containing all twelve primitive slots
split_outputs: data slots: D, Φ, T, Ω, K, f, H, P (destined for R0–R3)
witness-ancillary slots: R, Γ, Ç, Σ (excluded from the register file)
phase_2.fuse_element: the eight data slots written into R0–R3
phase_2.fuse_result: the identical IG tuple, because the data pairs alone uniquely determine the tuple’s identity in this computational context; the excluded slots are structurally redundant

phase_3.void_description: uninitialized register file with all eight registers set to N; the system before any tuple load or witness inscription
phase_3.true_description: a register pair encoding T in B4, indicating a successful evaluation or affirmative state, e.g., a slot combination that sums to 1 mod 4
phase_3.false_description: a register pair encoding F in B4, indicating a negative evaluation or failure, e.g., a slot combination that sums to 2 mod 4
phase_3.both_description: a register pair encoding B in B4, indicating a paradice where truth values are held simultaneously without resolution, e.g., a slot combination that sums to 3 mod 4

steps.domain_action: the register file is entirely void; no tuple, no witnesses, no vote. All R0–R7 hold N.
the IG tuple is loaded from the Grammar into the computational layer, moving from external specification to internal representation.
the tuple is decomposed into all twelve primitive slots. The T-arm collects the eight data slots (D,Φ,T,Ω,K,f,H,P); the F-arm collects the four witness-ancillary slots (R,Γ,Ç,Σ).
the F-arm immediately discards the ancillary slots; they are not written to the register file and are lost to the system. This branch terminates with an empty contribution.
the T-arm retains the eight data slots and confirms the architectural rule that only data pairs occupy R0–R3.

the eight data slots are recomposed into the original tuple, proving that the register file content suffices to reconstruct the tuple identity. The file now contains the clean tuple in its lower four registers.

the running program inspects itself and computes four closure witnesses: token diversity (written to R4 as a B4 value), self-reference (R5 as T/F), Frobenius order (R6 as T/F), and dialetheia completeness (R7 as T/F). R4–R7 transition from void to concrete witness states.
the substrate vote process begins, reading the register file to compute token affinities.
the vote yields a token score above the selection threshold, affirming the token that the substrate will synthesize into the next program.
the selected token is permanently recorded in append-only memory, creating an irreversible snapshot of the substrate’s decision.

the system boundary is sealed; the register file now contains both the tuple data (R0–R3) and closure witnesses (R4–R7), and the vote outcome is fixed. The adjoint and one-to-one never entered the file.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the MiniKernel’s substrate evaluator, which translates the IG tuple into a canonical program and seeds the register file
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: direct register access within the eight-wide B4 file; the token affinity table mediates between register states and program synthesis
phase_5.memory_mechanism: an append-only store for IFIX records, holding the sequence of token selections that build the program space
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the canonical program runs to completion, then triggers IMSCRIB and the substrate vote; execution is single-threaded and deterministic
phase_5.alfs_store: the Grammar’s canonical program repository, which provides the twelve-slot tuple definition and the closure witness computation functions

phase_6.cycle_cost: one register file read/write cycle per operation, plus the computational cost of split/merge and witness inscription
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: the register file is void (all N) before tuple loading, and the system has no closure evidence
phase_6.post_cycle_state: the register file contains the data tuple and computed witnesses; a token vote is recorded in memory. No information is lost because the tuple is fully recovered from the data slots and the witnesses are newly generated, not extracted from the tuple
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the transformation is reversible: the tuple is reconstructed exactly, and the closure witnesses are derived from the program structure, not consumed from the input entropy budget
